To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present the first crystal structure and biochemical characterization of a bacterial diphosphate diterpene synthase, and that this structure is used to rationally engineer this enzyme to produce new bioactive compounds.
the first crystal structure for a bacterial diterpenes cyclase has been determined and the structure-guided mutational approach led to the discovery of new diterpenes with biological activities.
the first structure of a diterpence cyclase was solved and the structure of the enzyme was correlated with its catalytic mechanism and product specificity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies for the production of complex natural products by metabolic engineering and the elucidation of the reaction mechanisms of the involved enzymes.
the structural and biochemical characterization of a diterpense cyclase and its mutants that are capable of producing a wide range of bioactive diterpenes.
the development of novel biocatalysts and the production of novel bioactive natural products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work presents a novel structure of a bacterial terpene synthase, the first structure of a diterpense cyclase, the first crystal structure with bound substrate, the first crystallographic evidence for the mechanism of action of terpene synthases and the first crystal structure that shows the plasticity residues that are responsible for product diversity.
this is a first report of the crystal structure of a diterpencyclase.
the structure of CotB2 is the first bacterial diterpence cyclase to be solved and that this structure has allowed the discovery of new antibiotics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have determined a high-resolution structure of CotB2, a bacterial diterpenoid cyclase, that has allowed us to understand the mechanism of diterpene biosynthesis and to engineer the enzyme in order to generate novel compounds with biological activity.

we have identified a new bioactive compound, (1R, 3E, 7E, 11S, 12S)-3-7-18-dolabellantriene, that is produced by CotB2(W286G) and we have solved the crystal structure of CotB2 at 1.6 Å resolution, which will help us to design future experiments to understand the mechanism of diterpene synthesis.
we have solved the first structure of a diterpense cyclase and that we have used this structure to design a mutant enzyme that produces a new bioactive diterpene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CotB2 is an enzyme that can be used to generate novel bioactive diterpenes, which are not found in nature.
CotB2 is the first bacterial diterpense cyclase to have its structure solved, which provides a structural framework to understand the reaction mechanism of diterpene biosynthesis.
CotB2 is an excellent target for metabolic engineering of diterpenes.
